segments.text: Here is the Hauser Mark Four—four core bays, each with an expandable theater display. Top bay: the Wideband Tuner scans six wavebands, four frequency maps, and expands full screen. Left bay: the Correlator decodes live cameras, phase plots, and cipher cartridges, then pops open. Center bay: Galactic Astrometry slews our phased-array beam, grades SINPO merit, and opens the Atlas. Right bay: the Verification Deck decodes slow-scan QSL cards and expands the hardware dossier.

segments.text: Now let's operate the Tuner, jumping across ninety-meter cryo-scatter, octal relays, and hydrogen masers. Spinning the vernier wheel slides the illuminated callsign scale and narrows the crystal passband filter. Next door, the frequency map cycles between spectrogram waterfall, band allocation, three-D ridges, and Doppler phase. Expanding the Band-Plan Scanner displays all six wavebands alongside intermediate-frequency passband zoom and Doppler lock.

segments.text: In the Correlator Bay on Callisto, we lock live arc-camera video and expand the Visual Theater. Tuning the Triangulum beacon in Three-D Spectrum mode pairs the hydrogen maser spike with a Lissajous rose. On Trojan Octal frames, Algorithm One faults, while Algorithm Two locks and translates the Euclidean telemetry. We pop open the full Cipher Theater, then audition the voice intercept and interval signal on the scope.

segments.text: In the Center Bay, tuning slews our phased-array beam while the twenty-segment S-meter and SINPO matrix lock. Expanding the Galactic Atlas reveals our Ceres Foundry parallax triangle, pulsar clock, and spiral-arm relay hops. In the Right Bay, triggering a Robot-Twenty-Four slow-scan burst wipes down line by line to decode the QSL card. Expanding the QSL Dossier reveals the subcarrier clue, while the memory tabs below cycle verified operator logs.

segments.text: In summary: the Mark Four pairs a six-band tuner and four-mode spectrum map with an expandable correlator. And it unites galactic beam triangulation and SINPO grading with slow-scan e-QSL dossiers and full-screen modals. Four bays, four expandable theaters, one complete deep-space DX workstation—seventy-three from Galactic Outpost Radio Nine.
